summary.title: Icosapent ethyl at a glance
points: Purified prescription EPA (Vazkepa), four 998 mg capsules a day with food; MAH now Recordati.
One indication: statin-treated high-risk adults with TG ≥1.7 mmol/L and either CVD or diabetes plus a risk factor.
Not a triglyceride drug: TG fell 18%, events 25%; benefit tracked EPA levels.
REDUCE-IT: MACE 17.2% vs 22.0% (HR 0.75); CV death HR 0.80; all-cause death not significant.
Watch bleeding, atrial fibrillation, soya/peanut allergy, fructose intolerance. Mixed omega-3 lost its post-MI use.

exercises.scenario: A pharmacist is asked to supply Vazkepa to lower triglycerides in a patient not on a statin.

questions.prompt: Does the licence cover it?
options: Yes, if triglycerides are above 5.6 mmol/L
Yes, as long as the patient has diabetes
Yes, it's a triglyceride-lowering medicine first and foremost
questions.explanation: Statin treatment is a requirement, and it isn't licensed simply to lower triglycerides.

questions.prompt: A 66-year-old on a statin, prior MI, TG 2.1 mmol/L. Does he fit?
options: No: Vazkepa is only for primary prevention
Yes: all the gates are met
questions.explanation: Adult, statin, high risk, TG ≥1.7, established CVD.

exercises.scenario: A colleague says 'omega-3s don't work: the EMA withdrew them for heart attacks'.

questions.prompt: What's the distinction?
options: The EMA withdrew Vazkepa in 2018 as well, along with every omega-3 product
That was mixed EPA+DHA at 1 g; Vazkepa has its own outcome trial

questions.prompt: What did REDUCE-IT show for death from any cause?
options: No data were collected on deaths
A significant 25% reduction in all deaths

summary.title: How it works
points: An ethyl ester de-esterified in the gut; EPA travels via the lymph; take with food.
Mechanisms 'not completely understood': fewer TG-rich particles, anti-inflammatory, plaque stabilisation, mild antiplatelet effect.
EPA may replace arachidonic acid in membranes, reducing pro-inflammatory eicosanoids.
Benefit tracked EPA levels, not TG or LDL response, but that's an on-treatment analysis.
Cleared by beta-oxidation; half-life about 89 hours; few CYP interactions.

exercises.scenario: A patient asks whether she can take the capsules on an empty stomach.

questions.prompt: What does the SmPC say?
options: Empty stomach is better because absorption is faster
Take them with or after a meal
Either way, since food has been shown to make no difference
Only at bedtime, to reduce the fishy aftertaste
questions.explanation: Every trial gave it with food, and none tested it without.

questions.prompt: Why are interactions few?
options: It's cleared unchanged by the kidneys without any metabolism
It binds to warfarin and inactivates it in the gut
It strongly induces CYP3A4, cancelling interactions
EPA is burned like dietary fat
questions.explanation: Beta-oxidation; CYP enzymes play a minor role.

exercises.scenario: A partner claims 'the higher your EPA level, the more you benefit, proven'.

questions.prompt: What's the caveat?
options: It's an on-treatment analysis, not randomised
The link went the other way
EPA levels weren't measured in REDUCE-IT, so the link is only modelled
questions.explanation: People reaching high levels may differ, for example in adherence.

questions.prompt: Why isn't Vazkepa really a triglyceride drug?
options: It was never tested in people with raised triglycerides
Benefit didn't track the triglyceride fall
It lowers LDL more than triglycerides

summary.title: History
points: Mixed omega-3 approved post-MI around 2000 on open-label GISSI-Prevenzione; EMA later removed that use.
Vazkepa (Amarin) approved in 2021 on its own trial, REDUCE-IT.
Mineral-oil placebo: LDL rose 10% on placebo vs 3% on drug.
Approval isn't access: about 20 reimbursement dossiers; Sweden 2022, Finland 2022.
2025: Recordati licensing deal for 59 countries ($25m upfront, up to $150m milestones); renewal January 2026.

exercises.scenario: You're reviewing the Amarin–Recordati deal as a BD case study.

questions.prompt: What did Recordati pay upfront?
options: Nothing upfront, only milestone payments later
$150 million, plus royalties on all sales
questions.explanation: Plus up to $150m in sales milestones, supply revenue and royalties.

questions.prompt: What's Recordati's role now?
options: MAH in the EU, with affiliates as local contacts
A manufacturer supplying Amarin's EU launches
Only a distributor, with Amarin still holding the licence
A co-promoter in Southern Europe only
questions.explanation: Recordati took over the EU licence.

questions.prompt: Choose the reason.
options: Different product and dose, with its own outcome trial

questions.prompt: What's the gap between EU approval and patient access?
options: A second EMA review for each country before any sale is allowed
questions.explanation: Some countries allow individual reimbursement first.

summary.title: What it's approved for
points: Five gates: adult, on a statin, high CV risk, TG ≥1.7 mmol/L, CVD or diabetes plus a risk factor.
REDUCE-IT: 71% established CVD, 29% diabetes plus risk factors.
Trial entry: TG from 1.53, LDL 1.03–2.59 mmol/L; high LDL wasn't studied.
Not covered: TG lowering alone, no statin, children, TG ≥5.64, PCSK9 users (excluded).
Omacor: triglyceride indication only (Fredrickson IV alone; IIb/III with a statin).

Excipients: maltitol, sorbitol, soya lecithin.
Bottles of 120 (30 days) or day-labelled blisters.
MAH Recordati; Recordati affiliates as local reps, except Vianex in Greece.
Same ATC code as Omacor (C10AX06): ATC is chemistry, not evidence.

summary.title: How it's taken
points: Two capsules twice a day with or after a meal, swallowed whole.
Missed dose: take when remembered; skip a fully missed day; don't double.
No dose change for kidneys, liver or age; check liver enzymes in liver impairment.
Monitor bleeding with antiplatelets or anticoagulants; watch for atrial fibrillation.
Avoid with soya/peanut allergy or fructose intolerance; caution with fish allergy; SmPC is the reference on breastfeeding.

summary.title: Reading a clinical trial
points: A placebo is still a comparator: REDUCE-IT used mineral oil, STRENGTH corn oil.
REDUCE-IT's placebo arm saw LDL, CRP and apoB rise; was part of the benefit placebo harm?
STRENGTH was stopped for futility in 2020.
Five-point and three-point MACE both fell about a quarter in REDUCE-IT.
Between-trial heterogeneity: product, placebo, patients and EPA levels all differed.

exercises.scenario: A competitor says 'REDUCE-IT was just a bad placebo'.

questions.prompt: What's a fair answer?
options: Disproven: the placebo was fully inert
It's an open question; biomarker shifts were small
Proven: the mineral oil explains the whole effect, as STRENGTH showed
questions.explanation: The EMA approved on REDUCE-IT; commentators want a neutral-placebo trial.

questions.prompt: Why did both MACE endpoints matter?
options: Three-point MACE was negative, so only softer events fell
The result didn't rest only on softer events
questions.explanation: Both fell by about a quarter.

exercises.scenario: Why can't REDUCE-IT vs STRENGTH be read as EPA vs EPA+DHA?

questions.prompt: Choose the reason.
options: Product, placebo, patients and EPA levels all differed

questions.prompt: What does 'stopped for futility' mean?
options: The drug was clearly harmful at the interim analysis
A benefit had become very unlikely
The trial ran out of money
questions.explanation: Decided by the data monitoring committee.

summary.title: The pivotal trials
points: REDUCE-IT: 8,179 on statins, mineral-oil placebo, 4.9 years; HR 0.75; 3-point MACE HR 0.74.
Placebo LDL rose 10% vs 3%; AF hospitalisation 3% vs 2%.
STRENGTH: 13,078, EPA+DHA 4 g vs corn oil; HR 0.99; stopped for futility; AF up.
Three candidate explanations: EPA alone, higher EPA levels, or placebo effect. None proven.
GISSI-Prevenzione (open-label, 1 g) underpinned the old mixed omega-3 approvals.

questions.prompt: Which statement is fair?

summary.title: Combination trials
points: The licence names one partner: a statin, required.
No SmPC lines for ezetimibe, PCSK9, BP medicines, SGLT2 or GLP-1; antithrombotics raise bleeding.
Evidence comes from REDUCE-IT's background: statins and BP well represented; ezetimibe 6.4%; PCSK9 excluded.
Diabetes subgroup: HR 0.77, no interaction (p = 0.29).
'No difference seen' with ezetimibe isn't 'shown to be the same'.

CV death HR 0.80; all-cause death HR 0.87, not significant.
NNT about 21 over 4.9 years; don't compare across modules.
Benefit similar above and below TG 1.7 mmol/L.

summary.title: Side effects
points: Bleeding 11.8% vs 9.9%; serious bleeding higher only with antithrombotics (3.4% vs 2.6%).
AF 5.8% vs 4.5%; 12.5% vs 6.3% with prior AF; seen across high-dose omega-3 trials.
Also oedema, constipation (placebo may confound), gout, rash, musculoskeletal pain.
Uncommon: allergy, fishy taste.
Contact a doctor for palpitations or bleeding that won't stop.

summary.title: Who shouldn't take it, and interactions
points: Contraindicated: allergy to icosapent ethyl, soya or peanut; avoid in hereditary fructose intolerance.
Caution: fish or shellfish allergy; liver impairment (monitor enzymes); prior AF.
No level interactions with omeprazole, rosiglitazone, warfarin or atorvastatin.
The practical interaction is bleeding with antiplatelets and anticoagulants.
Sorbitol about 332 mg/day: count with other sources.

summary.title: Pharmacovigilance
points: Additional monitoring (black triangle): report any suspected side effect.
RMP: two important identified risks (bleeding with antithrombotics, AF); no potential risks.
No PSUSA outcome or PRAC signal found in this module's search.
The 2018 omega-3 review removed an indication for lack of benefit, with no new safety issue.
A neutral-placebo outcome trial could strengthen or weaken the evidence.

questions.prompt: In your own words: why did the EMA remove mixed omega-3's heart indication but approve Vazkepa?
questions.modelAnswer: The mixed products' post-heart-attack approval rested on an open-label 1999 trial that later data didn't confirm, so the benefit wasn't shown. Vazkepa is a different product at a higher dose, and its approval rested on its own double-blind outcome trial, REDUCE-IT, which was positive.

summary.title: The label in practice
points: Five gates; trial entry was narrower than the label on LDL and TG.
Four capsules a day with food; sorbitol, maltitol, soya lecithin.
No dose changes; monitor bleeding, AF and liver enzymes where relevant.
Allergy and fructose rules; SmPC wins on breastfeeding.

summary.title: The evidence
points: REDUCE-IT positive (HR 0.75), including stroke and CV death; all-cause death not significant.
STRENGTH neutral (HR 0.99) with a different product and placebo.
Placebo debate unresolved; between-trial heterogeneity prevents a clean answer.
Combination evidence is indirect, from REDUCE-IT's background.

questions.prompt: In your own words: why is the choice of placebo oil so important here?
questions.modelAnswer: For oil capsules the placebo must also be an oil. If that oil isn't inert, the result measures the drug's effect plus any harm from the placebo. REDUCE-IT's mineral oil was linked to rises in LDL and CRP in the placebo arm, so part of the difference might come from the placebo group doing worse.
